A specialist returning a FINDING instead of a diff is a legitimate outcome, not a failure to route around. Rule on it, freeze the ruling as a contract decision in spec.md, and mark the task DROPPED in tasks.md with the evidence path so a post-context-reset spurt cannot re-attempt it.

A guard that stops an exception must not also stop the SIGNAL. When a fix converts a raise into a swallowed condition on a data-loss path, ask what the caller now sees and rule on it explicitly -- 'no longer raises' is not the same as 'no longer loses'. Added spurt 4 after spec.md C14: the #243 guard turned the owner's path from 'lost + raised' into 'lost + returns cleanly, one debug line', and 'log at debug level' in the task brief was the defect. Log anomalous states at ERROR, and prefer 'attempt everything, then fail loudly' over a quiet success.

Do not freeze an inferred INTERNALS mechanism as a contract decision on the strength of one black-box measurement. Enumerate the rival mechanisms, state which observations would distinguish them, and route it to a probe. Freeze only what was measured, plus inferences whose premises are named. Added spurt 4 (spec.md C13).

When a probe settles a mechanism question, freeze BOTH what it proves AND what it still cannot distinguish -- and freeze the SCOPE CEILING that follows, as its own contract item, in the loudest place available. Added spurt 5 (spec.md C16/C17): T6 confirmed mechanism (ii) and ruled out (i), but could not separate (ii) from (iii); recording that honestly cost nothing because both imply the same ceiling, and the ceiling -- 'no CloseProject()-side change can ever fix the filed incident' -- is the single fact the whole feature turns on. Corollary: a ceiling has two halves. State the fix that DOES hold (T3's P-3 path, 0/25 -> 25/25) in the same breath as the one that cannot; either half alone is a misrepresentation.

A detector must be validated against BOTH the failing and the succeeding case before a remedy is specified on it. Added spurt 5 (spec.md C18): C14 pre-emptively preferred a post-Save() IUndoStackManager 'has unsaved changes' read as 'mechanism-independent'; measured, it reads False in the 25/25 real-save AND the 0/25 no-op case -- indistinguishable, so the preference was void. And never word a diagnostic as more than it measured: HasUnsavedChanges == False means 'no completed-but-unsaved unit of work is registered', NOT 'there is nothing pending to save' (it read False while 25 entries still existed in memory).

Deferring a CHANGELOG entry is NOT a neutral hold once the code is on main. Added spurt 5 (spec.md C19): CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section accumulates until a version cut, so a shipped-but-unnoted public behaviour change would go out undocumented if a cut happened. Cost the 'wait' option explicitly, and prefer splitting out a minimal, factual stub describing SHIPPED behaviour (which commits the project to no position on any open ask, and has zero churn cost while it sits under [Unreleased]) over deferring the whole entry.
